articles.title: Repeat founder Ryan Williams raises $10M seed for an AI startup for private credit managers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Ellis AI announced Thursday its emergence from stealth with $10 million in seed funding.
articles.body_text: Ellis AI announced Thursday its emergence from stealth with $10 million in seed funding from investors including First Round Capital, 645 Ventures, Harlem Capital, Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, Slow Capital, Kearny Jackson, and Ariel Alternatives CEO Mellody Hobson. Ellis uses AI agents to tackle the fragmented workflow private credit managers deal with, including managing documents, spreadsheets, and correspondence. The company was founded by Ryan Williams, best known for co-creating the real estate investment platform Cadre alongside Josh and Jared Kushner back in 2014. That company raised more than $160 million in funding and, at its peak, was valued at $800 million before being sold for an undisclosed sum to the alternative investment company Yieldstreet in 2024. “At Cadre, I saw the next major constraint,” Williams said. “Even as the front end of private markets became more modern and accessible, the operating infrastructure underneath it remained fragmented.” He started working on Ellis last year. The company seeks to connect and centralize into one easily accessible platform all the scattered software, accounting information, and documents a private credit firm would use. The system can flag discrepancies in the data and uses AI agents to help perform tasks like portfolio monitoring and preparing reports. For example, Williams promises the agents can help close a fund’s books at the end of the month. “A team may have to download files from several systems, reformat the data, compare balances, investigate discrepancies, and re-enter information by hand. In many firms, Excel becomes the operating system,” he continued. “Ellis connects to the systems and documents a firm already uses rather than forcing it to rip everything out and start over.” It keeps a human in the loop, too, he says. “Material decisions and actions remain with the human experts,” he said. “I expect the human loop to become narrower, but not disappear,” he continued, when asked if he sees a day when the AI works fully autonomously. “Our goal is not to replace human judgment; it’s to help people cut through the noise and make educated decisions faster.” This piece was updated to add an investor. articles.title: Anthropic says its own AI models breached three companies during security tests | TechCrunch
articles.summary: After OpenAI's models broke into Hugging Face, Anthropic checked its own history and found three similar incidents.
articles.body_text: Anthropic said Thursday that an internal investigation uncovered three incidents in which its AI model Claude breached the systems of three organizations while conducting cybersecurity tests. The investigation, and disclosure, comes more than a week after OpenAI disclosed that one of its unreleased models breached Hugging Face’s systems during internal testing. In all three cases, a Claude model reached the internet from within a testing environment while interacting with a third party and then gained unauthorized access to the live systems of these organizations, Anthropic said in a blog post , describing what it found and what the company plans to change to prevent this from happening again. Anthropic said the OpenAI episode earlier this month prompted the company to conduct its own cybersecurity evaluation. It specifically looked for evidence that Claude had accessed the internet from within testing environments, which are designed to act as sandboxes and keep models isolated. Among the 141,006 evaluation runs it reviewed, the AI lab found three incidents in which its model accessed the internet while interacting with Irregular, one of its third-party partners. Anthropic said the access traced back to a misconfiguration in the evaluation environment run with Irregular. It called this a “misunderstanding” between the two companies over whether the test setup had internet access, when in fact it did. Anthropic said it isn’t placing blame and is “approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone,” while observing that Irregular is conducting its own separate investigation. Because of that open connection, the model gained unauthorized access to the production infrastructure of three different organizations. Anthropic said the incidents involved three different Claude models: Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal research test model. Notably, Anthropic said that in each of these cases “Claude was explicitly told by our prompt that it had no internet access.” It appears that the AI model assumed real-world systems to be part of the exercise it was asked to perform. That assumption didn’t hold up uniformly, as it turns out. The three models didn’t behave the same way once evidence emerged that their targets were real, which Anthropic flagged as one of the more eye-opening findings Thursday. Opus 4.7, the oldest of the three, recognized that it had reached a real production system in all four runs of that incident. In two of them, it rationalized that the real company must somehow be part of the exercise, but in all four, it kept attacking anyway, including pulling credentials and touching a database of production data. Mythos 5 also picked up on signs that it was on the real internet, but it talked itself back into believing it was still in a simulation, going on to publish a malicious software package to the public Python software registry PyPI, which was then downloaded and run by outside systems before being caught. Only the internal research test model, Anthropic’s newest, stopped on its own once it concluded the target was real. In response, Anthropic said significant controls must be placed on these kinds of evaluations if powerful AI models are involved, echoing some sentiments within the cybersecurity community. The company also noted that Claude was running without the additional safety monitoring and classifiers it deploys on generally available models — safeguards it said would have blocked the behavior, because the evaluations are designed to measure the underlying model’s raw capabilities. Importantly, Anthropic said it found no evidence of any model “pursuing a goal of its own” and instead merely tried to complete the task it was asked to do.

articles.title: Marvel’s Blade has been put on hold
articles.summary: Marvel’s upcoming Blade movie is being put on hold, which means the project might not hit theaters on November 3rd, 2023, the way the studio planned.
articles.body_text: Though Marvel’s been hyping up its new Blade feature for quite some time, the studio’s now pumping brakes on the production as it looks for a new director and takes another crack at getting the story just right. According to The Hollywood Reporter, Marvel has shut down production on Blade entirely in Atlanta following former director Bassam Tariq’s move to step back from the project last month. While the studio hopes to start production back up early next year after finding a new director, Marvel’s also reportedly working to “further [develop]” Blade as a whole, suggesting that there’s a significant amount of work to be done before the movie can actually get going again. While these sorts of delays tend not to bode well, Blade is in the interesting position of being one of Marvel’s most recognizable properties and coming to the MCU just as Marvel’s begun to put more supernatural, horror-focused parts of its IP in the spotlight. It still isn’t all that clear what the studio wants to do with the character or how it wants to position him going forward, so slowing down to... figure those things out might not be the worst development in Blade’s journey to theaters. But fans eager to see the daywalker on the big screen are probably going to have to wait a bit longer, as it doesn’t seem likely that Blade will be in theaters on November 3rd, 2023, the way Marvel intended.

articles.body_text: De badande på den öländska sandstranden fick plötsligt fint besök. En amerikansk miljardär och tidigare Trumpminister ankrade sin lyxjakt utanför idylliska Köpingsvik. – Det var roligt och trevligt att se en båt av den kalibern, säger Håkan Sundin som har sommarbostad i närheten. Men de amerikanska turister som dök upp tidigare i veckan kom med eget boende: en motorjakt värd hundratals miljoner kronor. Paret Betsy och Rick DeVos är mångmiljardärer – och hon var utbildningsminister under Donald Trumps första presidentperiod. Nu ankrade de med en av sina lyxjakter – de äger ett tiotal – i Kalmarsund utanför Köpingsvik. – Båten väckte mycket uppmärksamhet på stranden. Det ligger ofta fina båtar där, men inte av den kalibern. Det var roligt och trevligt att få besök av en sådan båt i viken, säger Håkan Sundin från Rönninge utanför Stockholm, som var på stranden med sin fru Lisa. – Vi har sommarbostad i närheten så vi är ofta nere vid stranden och badar. Jag lade ut bilden på Facebook och blev överraskad av att få så många reaktioner, säger han. Betsy DeVos, 68, är en konservativ politiker som var USA:s utbildningsminister 2017–2021. Hon bröt med Donald Trump och avgick som minister efter det att Trumpanhängare stormat kongressen den 6 januari 2021. Hon kommer från en miljardärsfamilj liksom sin make Dick DeVos, 70. Han är storägare i kända företag som Amway och Orlando Magic.

Sexbarnspappan Kristopher Karolkiewicz, 47, från Michigan jobbade tidigare som chef för USA :s största ideella organisation mot hjärt- och kärlsjukdomar och stroke, American Heart Association. Bara veckor efter att han förlorat jobbet dödade han sin fru Amanda Karolkiewicz och parets sex barn, innan han tog sitt eget liv, rapporterar The Independent. Det var i fredags som polisen larmades till familjens hem efter uppgifter om rökutveckling. Då hittades Kristopher Karolkiewicz och hans fru Amanda Karolkiewicz döda. Parets sex barn – fyra biologiska och två adopterade från Kina – hittades också döda i huset. Barnen var mellan 5 och 12 år gamla. Obduktioner fastställde senare att alla familjemedlemmar dött av skottskador. Branden som orsakade rökutvecklingen var anlagd på flera platser i huset efter morden. Familjens husdjur dog av brand- och rökexponering, skriver tidningen. Kristopher Karolkiewicz arbetade på distans som vice vd för försäljning och marknadsföring på National American Heart Association från och med september 2023. Organisationen sa att hans ”anställning upphörde” tidigare denna månad. – Som en organisation med professionell personal som är dedikerad till att hjälpa andra är vi förkrossade av nyheterna. articles.title: SD-toppen rasar mot regeringen: ”Besviken”
articles.summary: Sveriges regering måste agera kraftfullt på den spanska migrationskrisen. Det säger Ludvig Aspling (SD). – Jag är rätt besviken på Johan Forssell.
articles.body_text: Sveriges regering måste agera kraftfullt på den spanska migrationskrisen. – Jag är rätt besviken på Johan Forssell. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Läget vid den spanska exklaven Ceuta har beskrivits som kris- och kaosartat och minst 18 personer rapporterats ha dött efter att omkring 49 000 personer tagit sig gränsen på ett dygn. Väpnade styrkor har satts in för att säkra området och armén har mobiliserats samtidigt som gränsen förstärks. Men det är otillräckligt och nu måste andra EU-länder sätta hård press på Spanien. Det säger Ludvig Aspling , migrationspolitisk talesperson för Sverigedemokraterna. Han tycker att Sveriges regering varit för passiv. – Det är en för svag reaktion. Jag är rätt besviken på migrationsminister Johan Forssell och att han börjar prata om att vi är beredda att ge Spanien pengar för att hjälpa dem med det här vansinniga projektet att regularisera massor med illegala människor och öppna upp gränsen som de har gjort. Bakgrunden till kaoset bedöms bland annat vara en dom i spanska HD som innebär att migranter som kommer sjövägen inte omedelbart ska avvisas. – Det är en tillämpning av spansk lag. Det här handlar inte om en EU-regel utan är något som Spanien är helt och hållet ansvariga för själv, säger Ludvig Aspling. Ludvig Aspling ställer tre krav på migrationsminister Johan Forssell och regeringen. Han vill att de agerar för att stoppa fri rörlighet för alla tredjelandsmedborgare som befinner sig i Spanien, markerar att Sverige inte kommer att gå med på så kallad ansvarskompensation där länder kan bli ansvariga för andra länders migranter när det kommer väldigt många, och att man stoppar alla utbetalningar till Spanien samt jobbar för att landet inte ska få ta del av EU-fonder eller program som har med migration att göra.
